source.prompt: Instrumental background music for a classic 1990s-style Japanese fantasy role-playing game. The writing and orchestration evoke the golden age of 16-bit console RPG soundtracks (memorable singable lead melody, clear bass line, warm chords, tasteful hall reverb), but the production is high quality, warm and full, recorded with real-sounding instruments. Completely original melody. The game's world lives in an endless night lit by lanterns, lamps and great beacon fires; the score is gentle and melancholic, with warmth and a quiet, stubborn hope. A caravan camp in the desert at night: the fire has burned low, camels resting, an old caravan leader hums a star song his grandmother taught him. Intimate, tender and nostalgic, like an old lullaby under a huge sky. Tempo 76 BPM, 6/8 time, key of A minor to C major. Instrumentation: solo oud, gentle ney melody, soft frame drum, low cello, crackling-warm pads, tiny bells. Form: oud alone, ney sings the star song, cello answers, soft frame drum joins, song returns softer. Duration: 85 seconds. Instrumental only: no vocals, no singing, no spoken words, no lyrics. Keep one steady tempo and key from start to finish, no fade-in and no fade-out, no long silences; the last bar leads naturally back into the first bar so the piece loops seamlessly as game background music.
